# Retrospective

## Effective

Fresh independent sessions supplied distinct value: Sol isolated the early-input limitation, while Opus traced actual backend semantics and tested script signal targeting privately. Coordinator retained the scope limit rather than invent consensus or turn an explicitly scoped design into a regression. Both full reports and raw material evidence were read. No native desktop was necessary to support the narrow published claims.

## Deviations and corrections

Process-compliance flag is false. The first Opus plan failed missing-Node preflight without executing. Its history remains. Copying a hash-recorded binary into the second fixture enabled isolated runtime without host execution. Non-login bash deliberately replaced login bash to avoid host profile effects; public scope states this adaptation.

Fixture audit found accumulated postcondition/status mismatch handling instead of immediate stop, ungated diagnostic producers and pipeline members, omitted per-attempt polling records, incomplete transitive final-target assertions, and unguarded stub log writes/child status. No retained case mismatched and no failed prerequisite was detected in the material claims, but that does not establish full compliance. The reviewer withdrew overbroad guard coverage in a preserved addendum. Parent-root checks and namespace containment are not substitutes for required final-target assertions. No cleanup or deletion was used to hide failures.

Responsible future assignment instructions: before any fixture launch, inventory every callee, final write target, producer and expected status. Assert resolved final targets or explicitly label any unavoidable parent-only coverage and obtain correction before execution. Case/status and postcondition mismatch must stop the affected case immediately. Record all polling attempts uniquely. Gate each pipeline producer and logging stub. Never infer complete coverage from exit 0 or a seal. Tool preflight immediately follows init. Retain test adaptations and distinguish source reading, real process with specified stubs, string checks and native end-to-end execution. Full correction detail: reviewers/fable/addendum.md section 5.

## Tool notes and resources

Potential toolkit improvements, not confirmed bugs: init could check tool availability earlier; hash-pinned shared tool material could reduce duplicated Node evidence. No Omadev issue observed because none was used. Owned sandbox and child processes exited; private scratch namespace was torn down, with no global process discovery required for cleanup. Technical panes and native session history remain preserved and idle.

## Presentation

Small source-supported flow beside the outcome, explicit early-input boundary, and no unsupported native claims. Fresh editorial check gets only the exact draft and immutable privacy-inclusive requirements. Saved HTML must not be opened by the coordinator. Outer assistant alone handles freshness and publication.
comment:
**Verified:** No actionable defect found in the tested post-settle dismissal path at `71ebdbbcf4087`. The idle test passes, and an isolated command-level check matched the dismissal pattern to the real screensaver script rather than the terminal stand-in or launcher decoy. Signalling it ran its cleanup trap and requested cursor restoration.

The source also preserves a menu-launched screensaver's window tracking when an idle cycle starts. The intended flow is:

```text
Tracked screensaver window
  -> one second without input
  -> subsequent pointer input requests script termination
  -> window closure cancels the pending idle/lock cycle
```

This is a source-supported flow, not an observed desktop sequence. The one-second quiet period is a meaningful boundary: pointer motion starting before it elapses can keep resetting it. Dismissal then needs a pause followed by new input; continuous early motion does not itself cancel the pending lock.

---
## Review information

**Test scope:** Focused idle test, baseline/control checks and script signalling with synthetic terminal, compositor-command and animation stand-ins. The signal command used a non-login shell. Hyprland/Quickshell upstream source was inspected; installed-version compatibility, real pointer input, terminal behavior and end-to-end lock cancellation were not tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium performed initial inspection and synthesis, with independent technical assessments by Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh. Claims were checked against source and targeted evidence.
